Question 10(c) [15 marks]: Assess the features of the economy of Minoan Crete. Support your answer with reference to the following interpretation and other relevant sources. This wondrous world of wealth in the leading sector of Cretan Bronze Age societies is not representative of society as a whole. The picture of a benevolent* aristocracy redistributing its wealth to the lower classes is questionable . . . Some households produced and traded in basic necessities, probably at local markets, contrary to the belief that all economic activities were regulated by the central authority.
KOSTIS CHRISTAKIS ‘Minoan Society and Culture’ The Encyclopedia of Ancient History, 2012
* benevolent kind and generous

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 15):
13–15 marks: Provides a well-developed and reasoned judgement relevant to the question | Demonstrates detailed and accurate knowledge and understanding relevant to the question | Interacts with the interpretation provided and uses evidence from other relevant sources to support the response | Communicates effectively using a range of appropriate historical terms and concepts
10–12 marks: Provides a reasoned judgement relevant to the question | Demonstrates accurate knowledge and understanding relevant to the question | Refers to the interpretation provided and uses other relevant source(s) to support the response | Communicates clearly using appropriate historical terms and concepts
7–9 marks: Provides some judgement relevant to the question | Demonstrates knowledge and understanding relevant to the question | Refers to the interpretation provided and/or other source(s) | Communicates using some appropriate historical terms and/or concepts
4–6 marks: Demonstrates some knowledge and/or understanding relevant to the question | May refer to the interpretation provided and/or other source(s) | Communicates using some historical terms and/or concepts
1–3 marks: Makes general statement(s) relevant to the question | May refer to the interpretation provided and/or a source | May use some historical terms and/or concepts


ANSWERS COULD INCLUDE (the student does not need every point):
• Palace economy: The palace economy was an important feature, as it was part of the redistributive nature of the Minoan economy. Christakis refutes this, however, stating that the palace economies were an important feature for the way it privileged the upper classes.
• Agriculture was the most important feature as it formed the basis of the economy. Minoans cultivated olives, which contributed to the substantial oil and perfume industries, as well as grains and figs. Sheep were also kept, contributing to the Minoan textiles industry.
• Towns such as Gournia and Zakros were also important features, as they were centres for craft and industry. Evidence from these towns show their role in the production of textiles, metal work and pottery, contributing to trade, as mentioned by Christakis.
• Trade and economic exchange were substantial features of the Minoan economy. Minoans needed copper and tin, which were imported and used in their metalworking industry. In return, Minoans exported pottery, textiles, oil and other resources.
• Religious donations also were an important feature of the economy, with Linear B tablets indicating large scale contributions to temples/religious officials, indicating a one-way economy.
